info.title: Stripe Projects Public Site API
info.summary: Public discovery and preview endpoints exposed by projects.dev.
info.description:
Read-only endpoints used for discovery, health checking, and social preview rendering on projects.dev.

This is **not** the Stripe Projects product API. Provisioning, credential retrieval, and billing all happen through the Stripe CLI plugin (`stripe plugin install projects`); see https://docs.stripe.com/projects. These endpoints exist so that agents and monitoring tools can discover and verify the public website.

## Authentication

None. Every endpoint described here is public and unauthenticated, declared explicitly by the empty root-level `security` array. There are no OAuth scopes, API keys, or protected resources on this surface, so no authorization server metadata is published. See https://projects.dev/auth.md.

## Errors

Error responses use RFC 9457 problem details with the `application/problem+json` media type. Branch on the stable `code` field rather than on `title` or `detail`, which are human-readable and may be reworded.

## Versioning and deprecation

This document is versioned by `info.version` using semantic versioning. Paths are deliberately unversioned: the surface is read-only and changes additively. See the `x-deprecation-policy` extension below and https://projects.dev/developers/ for the full policy.

signals.description: Set on any endpoint scheduled for a breaking change.
HTTP-date after which the endpoint may stop responding.
Points at documentation explaining the change and its migration path.

get.description: Returns a 200 JSON body when the public site is serving. Intended for uptime checks and for agents confirming the host is reachable before following discovery links.

Cache-Control.description: Always `no-store`; health responses are never cached.

get.summary: Generate a stack share OG image
get.description: Renders the PNG social preview used for stack share links. An unrecognised or malformed `stack` value is not an error: the endpoint falls back to a generic card, because a broken image in a link unfurl is worse than a generic one. Callers that need to validate a stack payload should not rely on this endpoint's status code.

parameters.name: stack
parameters.description: Encoded stack share payload from a `/s/<payload>` URL, in the form `v1:<provider>~<service>,...`. Unknown providers are dropped.

200.description: A generated PNG image. Returned even when `stack` is absent or unparseable.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The HTTP method is not supported by this endpoint.

Allow.description: Comma-separated list of methods this endpoint accepts.

value.title: Method Not Allowed
value.detail: This endpoint only supports GET and HEAD. Received POST.

Health.description: Health report for the public site.

status.description: Always `ok`. An unhealthy site does not return this body.

time.description: RFC 3339 timestamp at which the response was generated.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details, served as `application/problem+json`. Branch on `code`, which is stable, rather than on `title` or `detail`, which are human-readable and may be reworded without a version bump.

externalDocs.description: RFC 9457 — Problem Details for HTTP APIs

type.description: URI identifying the problem type. Dereferences to documentation for this error.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary of the problem type.

status.description: HTTP status code, duplicated in the body so the problem survives logging.

code.description: Stable, machine-readable error identifier. This is the field to branch on.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation specific to this occurrence, including a resolution hint where one exists.
detail.example: This endpoint only supports GET and HEAD. Received POST.

instance.description: URI reference identifying the specific occurrence, i.e. the request path.
